newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end up 3/8 to 1/2.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end up 3/8 to 1/2.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended 3/8 to 1/2 point higher as players took heart from a drop in April producer prices, but were reluctant test loftier levels ahead of Thursday's consumer price index data.

"Everybody's a little concerned going in at these high levels," one trader said, adding that he saw some afternoon selling pressure. "There's a couple of people looking to get out going into the number tomorrow."
Economists polled by Reuters expect April CPI to rise 0.1 percent overall. They expect the core rate, which excludes food and energy prices, to rise 0.2 percent.

On Wednesday, the producer price index showed a 0.6 percent drop, versus the unchanged reading economists had predicted. The core rate printed down 0.1 percent, while expectations called for a 0.1 percent rise.
A municipal analyst judged the overall muni cash market up 3/8 to 1/2 a point, with high-grade issues improving by three basis points.
Dollar bonds rose 1/4 of a point following the PPI report, were up 3/8 to 1/2 by noon, and were quoted in a range thereafter. Moderate morning activity gave way to light afternoon action.
"The Treasuries stopped, we stopped and they said 'Well, don't forget tomorrow is CPI so let's get through that one without pushing this any further,'" the analyst said.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 16/32 at 96-23/32 in late New York trade. In debt futures, the June municipal contract closed up 15/32 at 116-2/32. The June T-bond contract closed up 11/32 at 110-5/32. The MOB spread was 189 ticks.
New issue pricing was firm to strong, the analyst said.

Negotiated action saw Smith Barney Inc reprice and restructure Cook County, Illinois' $206 million general obligation bond issue, adding maturities in 2018 and 2019, and raising the top yield in 2022 to 5.82 percent from 5.80 percent.
Lehman Brothers repriced $115.7 million Los Angeles County, Calif., lease revenue bonds. The top yield was 5.71 percent in 2029.
Looking ahead to Thursday, municipal bond sales are expected to total $371 million in 23 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $274 million in 12 sales, with a $79 million Lorain County, Ohio, variable rate bond deal through Bear, Stearns & Co. topping the list.
